title: We just shipped a feature that helps game masters share their adventures with more people than ever before!
author: katsuthunder
selftext:
Hey there! I've been lurking in this sub for a while. Super cool to see all of the awesome things people are making.

I'm one of the developers of [Friends & Fables](https://fables.gg/). We're an AI RPG platform. Most other AI RPGs out there are just a simple chat with an AI game master experience. We've got an AI game master as well, but we're especially focused on making creator tools so that folks can easily build out their own worlds and adventures.

I'm excited to announce that we've just shipped Quests and One-shots. To our users, this is a way for them to write out stories and adventures, but under the hood, it is actually a no-code way to program our game engine. I put together a video to explain how it works, and you can also read the full details in this [blog post](https://feedback.fables.gg/changelog/a-new-creative-medium-friends-and-fables-quests-and-one). The tl;dr is that we have a database that holds all of your game state, a game engine that converts that state into context and a cohesive framework for LLMs, and various agents to interact with game state and handle player actions. This quest system is a way for people to program in game state updates and time them with narrative beats.

If you're curious to experience one of these adventures, check out our first [official one-shot here](https://play.fables.gg/one-shots/0197ec14-5d56-7964-a557-7d69c32bd8d2). You can play it for free, no credit card required. You do get paywalled after 50 turns because AI is expensive to run, but you can refresh more turns each day.

This is my first time posting here, so if anyone has any questions about Friends & Fables and our development, I'm happy to answer them!

https://reddit.com/link/1lvoroj/video/uv5r1qe2tvbf1/player

comments.author: interestingsystems
comments.body: This looks great, I'm looking forward to running through the one-shot. I'm interested in how Franz handles player direction that cannot be classified into one of the paths that has been defined. Does it basically stop the player from doing anything else, irrespective of how creative they manage to be? I don't mean this as a criticism - I can't think of a better solution, but I'm curious to know if you guys have worked out a different approach.

replies.author: katsuthunder
replies.body: That's something we're still working on right now, for now quest builders can write fallback paths, but what we're working on is progressively updating future steps!

replies.author: interestingsystems
replies.body: Oooh, that's pretty smart. Looking forward to seeing where you take this. Great job with Friends & Fables in general.
